On the 1492 and 1783 maps, Sind is the lower Indus valley as a state of its own, ruled first by the Sammas and later by Mughal governors and local dynasties.

In 1492 the Samma dynasty ruled from Thatta, which grew rich on the river trade and on cloth. Jam Nizamuddin II, who reigned until 1508, is remembered as a just king. The Sammas and the nobles of Thatta filled the Makli necropolis with carved stone tombs.

In 1520 the Arghuns, Turko-Mongol lords pushed out of Kandahar by Babur, conquered Sind. In 1591 Akbar annexed it to the Mughal Empire. As the Mughals weakened, the Kalhoras ruled Sind and paid tribute to Ahmad Shah Durrani. In 1783, the year of the later map, the Baloch Talpurs overthrew them; Britain conquered their emirates in 1843. See Sindh for the earlier centuries.
sum: On the 1492 and 1783 maps, Sind is the lower Indus valley as a state of its own, ruled first by the Sammas and later by Mughal governors and local dynasties.
